sections.heading: C — Licensing and required documents
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing and required documents

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
A Class D basic license covers a non-commercial vehicle weighing less than 26,000 pounds gross vehicle weight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
A first Montana license normally requires vision, written and road testing, although a valid license from another jurisdiction may remove the testing requirement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Drivers must keep their valid Montana driver license with them when driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
The vehicle being driven must carry evidence of liability insurance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
The application name and birth date must agree with the primary identity document and are checked against Social Security Administration records. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
A Montana driver license or identification-card application requires the applicant’s Social Security number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
A traffic education permit allows a student enrolled in an approved course to drive during training under a traffic education instructor’s direct supervision. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A02
The traffic education permit remains valid only while its holder is enrolled in the course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
A person aged at least 14½ may obtain a learner permit through participation in, or successful completion of, traffic education approved by the Department of Justice and Superintendent of Public Instruction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
A Class D learner-permit driver needs an accompanying licensed instructor, parent or legal guardian, or another adult authorized by the parent or guardian, seated beside the driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
Without traffic education, a learner-permit applicant must be at least 16 years old. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
At age 15, a learner-permit applicant must have successfully completed an approved driver education course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Obtaining a learner permit requires the identity, authorized-presence and Montana-residence documents, licensing fees, and successful written and vision tests at an exam station. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Before a teenage applicant under 18 may begin testing, a parent, guardian or responsible adult must sign the consent form. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
Signing the minor’s consent form makes the parent, guardian or responsible adult financially responsible for damage from the minor’s driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
The learner-license permit is issued after the primary written test for that license type is passed and lasts one year. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
A new driver under 18 must use the non-commercial learner permit for six consecutive months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
Traffic education courses must have approval from both the Office of Public Instruction and the Department of Justice. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
Online and third-party traffic education courses do not qualify as approved traffic education. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
A Montana resident with a valid driver license from another jurisdiction cannot receive a Montana identification card. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A02
A person must choose a state identification card or a driver license rather than hold both. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
A suspension or revocation in another state or jurisdiction prevents applying for, receiving or keeping a Montana driver license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A03
An applicant aged 18 or older must supply acceptable proof of authorized presence, identity and residency. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A03
Adult applicants must surrender their other driver licenses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A03
Adult applicants must satisfy the medical requirements for the requested license type. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A03
An adult applicant must not have a court finding of mental incompetence, alcoholism or habitual illegal-drug use. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A03
Minor applicants need consent from a parent, guardian or responsible adult who accepts financial responsibility. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A03
After establishing permanent Montana residency, a driver with a valid license from the former jurisdiction may use it for up to 60 consecutive days before surrendering it and qualifying for a Montana license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A03
A driver carrying a valid out-of-state basic license may exchange it for a Montana license without written or road testing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A03
Applicants whose functional ability to drive safely may be impaired can be required to take written and road tests. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A03
A person may hold only one valid driver license across all licensing jurisdictions at a time. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A04
Active-duty service members and their dependents may drive on a valid out-of-state license unless they become gainfully employed in Montana. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A04
A service member or dependent who becomes employed must obtain a Montana driver license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A04
An eligible service member presenting an active-duty military card can receive a license bearing a military exemption. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A04
A holder of the military exemption may apply to renew during military service outside the usual renewal window. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A04
A military-exempt license remains usable for up to 90 days after honorable separation from service. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A04
Proof of authorized presence means showing United States citizenship or federal authorization to be in the country. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A04
Montana verifies a foreign national’s authorized presence through the federal Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements system. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A04
A temporarily authorized foreign national’s license cannot extend beyond the expiration of that person’s official USCIS document. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A04
An original or certified birth certificate from a United States jurisdiction is acceptable evidence of authorized presence. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A04
For authorized presence, a State Department or United States embassy report of a citizen’s birth abroad may use form FS-240 or DS-1350. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A04
A valid, unexpired United States State Department passport or passport card may establish authorized presence. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F43 | anchor: A04
A valid, unexpired foreign passport may establish authorized presence when accompanied by a same-name USCIS I-94 with an unexpired nonimmigrant endorsement, or an unexpired permanent-resident I-551 stamp. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F44 | anchor: A04
For authorized-presence proof, a naturalization certificate must be valid and unexpired and use form N-550, N-570 or N-578. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F45 | anchor: A04
A valid, unexpired citizenship certificate on form N-560, N-561 or N-645 may establish authorized presence. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0014]

Misconceptions: A supervised course permit and a general learner permit have different conditions; keep their requirements attached to the permit type.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: name, presence, residence; then check the applicable document category.
Glossary: Class D; non-commercial learner permit; traffic education permit; primary document; secondary document; authorized presence.
Dynamic facts: Fee amounts, license-duration conflicts, historical REAL ID dates and station-specific appointment instructions are withheld as debt; use current issuer evidence before asserting them.
